name: views/auth.py
summary: DRF API views exposing user authentication endpoints (register, login, logout) with input validation, rate limiting, and service-layer delegation.
purpose: Acts as the HTTP controller layer for the user authentication lifecycle, isolating web transport concerns from domain logic by delegating to AuthService, thereby enforcing clean architecture and reusable authentication flows.
responsibilities: Expose REST endpoints for user registration, login, and logout operations
Validate incoming request payloads using dedicated per-action serializers
Delegate authentication business logic to AuthService to maintain thin controllers
Enforce rate limiting via AnonRateThrottle and UserRateThrottle
Apply DRF permission classes such as IsAuthenticated to protect sensitive endpoints
Return standardized HTTP/JSON responses with appropriate status codes
inputs: HTTP POST requests containing user credentials, registration data, or session/tokens
Validated request data from RegisterSerializer, LoginSerializer, and LogoutSerializer
outputs: HTTP JSON responses containing authentication tokens, user data, or structured error messages
HTTP status codes indicating the success or failure of authentication operations
architecture_notes: Implements the Controller layer in a layered architecture using Django REST Framework's APIView. Follows the Thin Controller / Fat Service pattern by delegating all business logic to AuthService. Uses dedicated per-action serializers for strong input validation and clear contracts. Applies DRF throttling (AnonRateThrottle for unauthenticated endpoints, UserRateThrottle for authenticated ones) and permission classes (IsAuthenticated) for defense in depth. This design promotes separation of concerns, high testability, and keeps the view layer focused solely on HTTP transport concerns.
improvements: Add explicit Python type hints to view methods and request handlers for better static analysis and maintainability
Introduce a BaseAuthView class to consolidate shared throttle classes, permission classes, and common response formatting across RegisterView, LoginView, and LogoutView
Add structured security audit logging for authentication events (failed logins, successful registrations, logouts)
Apply @extend_schema or equivalent OpenAPI decorators to improve API documentation and client discoverability
Implement centralized exception mapping so that AuthService exceptions are consistently translated to HTTP responses without repetitive try/except blocks in each view
Consider enforcing explicit parser_classes and renderer_classes to lock the contract to JSON-only inputs/outputs
